description:
Nova Squad is a crew of dreamers, creators, coders, and storytellers turning big space ideas into experiences. 
We’re here to break down the impossible, build the unexpected, and make exploring the cosmos feel a little more epic.
Welcome aboard!
summary: The Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer challenge asks participants to translate complex aerospace constraints into interactive experiences that teach kids ages 7–12 the real trade-offs of deep-space survival. To achieve this, we developed ASTRA-1: The Red Frontier, a browser-based interactive game modeled after NASA’s 378-sol CHAPEA Mars Dune Alpha habitat. Stepping into the boots of Cadet Nova in Arcadia Planitia, players navigate a 10-mission campaign featuring 30 interactive engineering activities balancing solar power against life support loads, scrubbing CO2, purifying graywater, and managing emergency countdowns. Rather than relying on fabricated statistics, our solution is powered directly by official NASA open data: NASA Open APIs and Curiosity/Perseverance telemetry establish realistic Martian surface pressures and dust optical depths; NASA OSDR data grounds hydroponic dwarf wheat cultivation; and live DONKI Space Weather alerts alongside RadLab radiation dose rates drive Solar Particle Event emergencies. This hands-on simulation matters because it moves beyond passive trivia, letting young learners experience firsthand how NASA mission planners solve compounding survival challenges.
details:
Project Overview

ASTRA-1: The Red Frontier is an interactive, browser-based Mars mission interactive game designed primarily for children aged 7–12. It transforms complex concepts of space exploration and Mars habitat engineering into an engaging, educational gaming experience.

What does it do and how does it work?

Players take on the role of Cadet Nova, a member of a five-person crew operating a fictional Mars habitat in Arcadia Planitia. Across a sequential 378-sol campaign, players complete 10 missions containing 30 interactive activities.

Players must manage essential habitat systems, including electrical power, oxygen supply, CO₂ removal, water reclamation, food production and radiation protection. They encounter realistic mission challenges such as global dust storms, life-support failures and solar particle events. Resources are interconnected, meaning decisions affecting one system can influence the performance of others.

The game includes interactive tasks, emergency scenarios, resource monitoring, crew interactions, and mission progression. It also incorporates NASA space science information, including live space-weather information from NASA's DONKI API and curated scientific references.

What benefits does it provide?

  • Makes complex space science and engineering concepts easier to understand.
  • Develops critical thinking, problem-solving and decision-making skills.
  • Introduces resource management and engineering trade-offs.
  • Allows students to learn through interactive experiences rather than passive reading.

What is the intended impact?

Our aim is to make space education more accessible, engaging and inspiring for younger generations. We want children to understand not only the excitement of space exploration but also the science, engineering and decisions behind it.

By turning real-world challenges into interactive missions, ASTRA-1 encourages curiosity about STEM fields and inspires young learners to become future scientists, engineers and explorers.

Tools and Technologies Used

  • HTML, CSS and JavaScript – Web development.
  • Canvas 2.5D – 3D game environment.
  • Three.js and WebGL – 3D elements.
  • NASA DONKI API – Live space-weather information.
  • NASA resources – CHAPEA, OSDR, Curiosity RAD and Perseverance MEDA.

    Additional resources considered during development include:
  • Google Antigravity – AI-assisted software development.
  • GitHub – Source-code management and version control

What makes the project creative and innovative?

ASTRA-1 combines storytelling, space science and resource-management gameplay. Players experience the consequences of their decisions through interconnected habitat systems, missions and emergencies, turning failures into learning opportunities.

Factors Considered During Development

  • Scientific relevance: Inspired by NASA research and Mars exploration challenges.
  • Age accessibility: Simplifying complex concepts for children.
  • Educational value: Teaching practical STEM concepts.
  • Gameplay: Balancing learning, storytelling and challenges.
  • Accessibility: Browser-based with no specialised hardware required.
  • Accuracy: Distinguishing real NASA information from simulated scenarios.

ASTRA-1 turns the challenges of living on Mars into an interactive learning experience where every decision matters and every mission teaches.
